headline: GitLab fixed a critical flaw in the AI Gateway behind its Duo Agent Platform that could let a logged-in user run commands on self-hosted servers.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 2: the flaw was disclosed on 2 Oct 2026 and carried in our 3 Oct edition, so this 10 Oct re-report is old news.
importance_line: Companies that run their own GitLab AI Gateway must update to stop a logged-in user from running commands on it, customers on GitLab-hosted gateways need do nothing, and the advisory does not say whether the flaw has been exploited.
summary: The Hacker News reports that GitLab disclosed on 2 Oct 2026 a critical flaw (CVE-2026-90970, rated 9.9 out of 10) in the AI Gateway that connects a GitLab installation to AI models, which could let a logged-in user with Duo Agent Platform access escape a protective sandbox (a walled-off area for running code) and execute commands on the server. Only organisations that host their own gateway must update, to version 19.2.4, 19.3.2 or 19.4.1, and the advisory does not say whether the flaw has been exploited; this is the flaw our 3 Oct 2026 edition already carried, so nothing here is new today.
notes: Older news re-dated: the pool item is a SecNews.gr page dated 10 Oct 2026, which showed only a security check page, so its text was not read. Read The Hacker News (2 Oct 2026) on the same flaw and credited it. Our 3 Oct 2026 edition carried BleepingComputer's report of the same advisory.
